a.summary: The EXTENSION_NAMES index is no longer bounded by the same value that gates the UnknownTokenExtension fallback, so a dispatch case added past index 28 turns a valid on-chain account into an ArrayIndexOutOfBoundsException escaping Token2022.read.
a.failure_scenario: Pre-commit, one value (`extensionTypes.length`) both gated the Unknown fallback and bounded the array read, so the index was structurally safe, and the enum switch had no `default` arm — adding a constant to ExtensionType was a compile error until a case arm was added. Post-commit the fallback is `default ->` while EXTENSION_NAMES is an independent 29-element literal list. Concrete drift: SPL ships extension 29, a maintainer follows AGAVE_SYNC.md step 4 and adds `NewExt.ordinal() { return 29; }` plus `case 29 -> NewExt.read(data, i)` but omits the EXTENSION_NAMES entry (nothing forces it — the array is private, its length is asserted nowhere, and `check` compiles clean). Parsing any mainnet mint carrying type 29 then reaches line 117 with extensionType=29 and throws `ArrayIndexOutOfBoundsException: Index 29 out of bounds for length 29` out of `Token2022.read` — an undeclared unchecked exception on a well-formed account, instead of the parsed extension. The pre-commit code could not produce this failure at all.

b.summary: Replacing the exhaustive enum switch with an int switch plus a parallel `EXTENSION_NAMES` array turns one compiler-enforced source of truth for extension wire IDs into three hand-maintained ones, and makes the name lookup an unguarded array index.
b.failure_scenario: SPL adds extension type 29 and a maintainer follows AGAVE_SYNC.md step 4: they add the record to the sealed hierarchy, give it `ordinal() { return 29; }` and add `case 29 -> Foo.read(data, i);` to the dispatch, but forget to append "Foo" to EXTENSION_NAMES. Nothing fails to compile. The first mint account carrying that extension reaches line 117, `EXTENSION_NAMES[29]` throws ArrayIndexOutOfBoundsException, and `Token2022.read`/`Token2022Account.read` blow up on real on-chain data with an exception type callers cannot distinguish from a bug. The mirror-image slip - adding the record and its `ordinal()` but forgetting the dispatch case - also compiles silently and degrades the extension to `UnknownTokenExtension`, whereas before the commit javac rejected a non-exhaustive `switch (type)` over the enum. Neither slip is caught by the test suite: `ExtensionEdgeCaseTests.firstUnsupportedAccountAndExtensionTypes` hard-codes 29 as the first unknown ID, and SolanaUpstreamLayoutConformanceTests only covers the 29 rows the frozen TSV already contains.

instructions.question: How does the defect described by `b` relate to the defect described by `a`?
instructions.focus: Compare the defects, not the wording. Two findings about the same code can still be different defects.

criteria: Different defects: fixing the defect `a` describes would leave the defect `b` describes unfixed, even when both sit in the same code.
The same underlying defect, but `b` narrows it, re-scopes which instances or inputs it covers, or reports it at a different place. Not a different defect in adjacent code.
The same defect restated in different words: fixing one fixes the other.

claims_new_evidence.instructions: Does `b` cite evidence that `a` does not?

criteria.true: `b` names a file, test, command, observation, or reproduction that `a` does not mention.
criteria.false: `b` cites nothing beyond what `a` already cites, or cites nothing at all.
